analysis.title: IG Looks Fine, Positioning Doesn't: Goldman's Three Credit Hedges For When Spreads Finally Catch Up
key_insights: US investment grade index yield is 6.51%, the highest on any lookback to 2004, while IG cash spreads are 82 bps, tighter than 92% of that history.

Goldman's October Macro Credit Hedge Menu says IG spreads stayed resilient, with rates rather than credit driving cash underperformance. Generic IG cash spreads are roughly unchanged from the start of September.
Goldman says credit vol continues to screen the cheapest across asset classes.

Valuations are stretched: IG at the 7th percentile, BBBs at the 6th, single-Bs at the 12th, leveraged loans at 288 bps in the 1st percentile (tighter than 99% of readings since 2013). CCCs are the exception at 992 bps, the 80th percentile.

Goldman's monitor as of Monday's close: IG spreads 2 bps wider on the month, BBBs 3 bps wider, CCCs 117 bps wider in a month and 214 bps in three months, at the 99th percentile of the past year and the 100th of the past three.

GS's Rich Privorotsky cites an FT chart showing CCC-and-lower yields up more than 4 percentage points since end-2025, over 3 points from spread and about 1 from Treasuries. He says higher rates increasingly hit SMEs and consumers, so the median corporate is a different story from the index.

Hedge 1: short GSIG30NH (30-year IG basket excluding hyperscalers) via total return swap, hedged with Treasuries. Catalysts are IG supply catching up and long-end rates selling off. Ex-hyperscaler spreads have widened only a little so far.
The September version paired this short with selling CDX IG 10Y protection and was carry-positive. The October version drops the CDX leg, making it an outright short with negative carry.

On $500M notional the short costs $7.6M a year, or 13.1 bps of widening to break even over 12 months (3.3 bps over three months). Basket spread is 101 bps. Approximate P&L is about $583K per bp: a 50 bp widening is worth about $27.3M, 100 bps about $51.9M, and a 20 bp tightening costs about $11.8M. Max loss is notional.

Bloomberg's credit daybook expected October to be the slowest issuance month of the year, with about $100B of high-grade supply projected and only $4.6B through Monday. This works against Hedge 1's supply catalyst.

Hedge 2: CDX IG 3-month implied vol is 40.7%, the 14th percentile since 2010, while the index is at 59 bps (91st percentile of the past year, about 9 bps wider in a month). Goldman moved from outright payers to a payer spread because payer skew steepened.

Payer spread structure: IG47 Dec 60/75 PS at 12.75 ref 58, 35 days, 5.2x gross and 4.2x net. $1M of premium buys about $784M of protection that starts paying around 62 to 63 bps and caps near $4.25M at 75 bps. CDX IG's one-year wide is 67.5 bps and three-year wide is 82 bps.

Hedge 3: buy $25M of CDX IG47 0-3% equity tranche protection at 31.328 points upfront, delta-hedged, to express single-name dispersion. Realized correlation has fallen over the past month against a stable implied correlation, which is near the top of its range since 2020.

Goldman cites more frequent idiosyncratic headlines and older index names becoming more vulnerable. The article ties this to Oracle bonds at a record low (Sep 25), Paramount Skydance bonds at 77 cents after a Fitch downgrade, and the largest high-yield deal on record.
The dispersion hedge moved from high yield (CDX HY junior mezz and super senior in September) to investment grade equity tranche in October.
Positioning: non-dealer net positioning in CDX is near all-time highs, roughly $125B in IG and $26B in HY by the author's chart read.
BofA warned that rates jitters are hitting flows into bond markets, with government bond, money market and high-yield funds all seeing outflows.

GS GOAL Kickstart says the credit component of its Risk Appetite Indicator recorded one of its sharpest weekly declines since 2000. Goldman's 12-month stance is overweight equities, underweight credit.

The ZeroHedge author argues credit is already cracking from the bottom, citing CCCs distressed for the first time since the 2023 bank crisis and a roughly $120B fallen-angel candidate that would enlarge the junk market by 10%. This is the author's view, not Goldman's.

trade_ideas.description: Short GSIG30NH (30-year IG basket ex-hyperscalers) via total return swap, hedged with Treasuries, $500M notional
trade_ideas.rationale: The basket screens attractive for a short, since supply from the broader IG issuer base and further long-end rate selling would widen spreads, and ex-hyperscaler spreads have widened only a little.
trade_ideas.risk: Negative carry of $7.6M a year; max loss is notional; a 20 bp tightening costs about $11.8M.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDX IG47 Dec 60/75 payer spread, 12.75 ref 58, 35 days, 5.2x gross and 4.2x net
trade_ideas.rationale: Payer skew has steepened, so the spread is a cheaper way to protect against moderate widening in cheap credit vol.
trade_ideas.risk: Protection is capped at 75 bps, so it does not cover a move beyond the year's worst day.

trade_ideas.description: Buy $25M CDX IG47 0-3% equity tranche protection at 31.328 points upfront, delta-hedged
trade_ideas.rationale: Realized correlation has dropped against a stable implied correlation, so the trade profits if a few names go badly wrong while the index average holds.

risk_factors: Rates, with a 5.3% 10Y and long-end selloff, are pressuring weaker borrowers such as SMEs and consumers.
Spreads are at extreme tights, so they offer little cushion against repricing.
CCC credit is already in distress, with spreads wide and still moving.
Idiosyncratic downgrades such as Oracle and Paramount Skydance, and a roughly $120B fallen-angel candidate, could enlarge the junk market.
Crowded non-dealer CDX positioning raises the risk of disorderly moves if investors rush to hedge or exit.
Outflows from government bond, money market and high-yield funds, and a sharp fall in the credit component of GS's Risk Appetite Indicator.
Slow October IG supply could delay the catalyst for the ex-hyperscaler short.

vol_and_positioning: CDX IG 3-month implied vol is 40.7%, the 14th percentile since 2010, and credit vol screens cheapest across asset classes.
Payer skew has steepened back up, leading Goldman to prefer a payer spread over outright payers.

Hedge ideas: short GSIG30NH ex-hyperscaler basket, IG47 Dec 60/75 payer spread, and long delta-hedged CDX IG47 0-3% equity tranche protection.
cross_bank_references: BofA warned late last month that rates market jitters are having a direct impact on flow strength into bond markets.
Bloomberg's Tuesday credit daybook expected October to be by far the slowest month of the year for IG supply.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says IG spreads stayed resilient, with rates driving cash weakness. Leveraged loans sit in the 1st percentile, so some investors keep taking credit risk at tight levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Spreads are at extreme tights, CCC spreads are at the 99th to 100th percentile of recent history, the median borrower is stressed, non-dealer positioning is near record highs and hedges are cheap.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slow October IG supply (about $4.6B through Monday against a projected $100B) would undercut the supply catalyst for the ex-hyperscaler short.

theme_stances.key_argument: Spreads are tight and credit vol is cheap while rates rise and weak borrowers are stressed, so hedges are attractive.
theme_stances.evidence: credit vol continues to screen the cheapest across asset classes
